brand.title: IQVIA (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — Introduction to CTFS - For TechIQ Attendees

questions.question: How many modules make up the CTFS platform?
choices: Three modules
Four modules
Five modules
Six modules
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—GrantPlan, Connect, Contracting, Forecasting, and Site Payments are the five modules that form the unified CTFS backbone.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The slide lists five distinct modules that work together as one platform. Knowing these five is essential for positioning CTFS as a complete solution.

questions.question: What is the primary pain point that Gilbert, the Clinical Operations Director, is trying to solve?
choices: Compliance risk and integration headaches
Manual financial drag and delayed site payments
Unpredictable cash flow and invoicing errors
Proof of AI effectiveness in production
questions.feedback_correct: You've nailed Gilbert's world—his frustration centers on the manual processes that slow payment cycles and leave sites unhappy.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While all of these are real pain points, they belong to different personas. Gilbert is the Clinical Operations Director focused on trial execution and payment speed.

questions.question: What is the shortest version of the CTFS pitch you should be able to deliver?
choices: Under 75 words for a five-minute chat
Under 150 words for a formal meeting
Under 35 words for a hallway conversation
Under 200 words for a detailed explanation
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—you've identified the hallway version, which is designed for quick, moving conversations where you have about 30 seconds.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course teaches three pitch lengths: 35 words for hallway, 75 words for five-minute conversations, and 150 words for formal meetings. The shortest is always for hallway situations.

questions.question: According to the course, when does CTFS Contracting reach general availability?
choices: End of September
End of November
End of December
End of October
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the module reaches general availability at the end of November, which is why everyone at TechIQ will be asking about it.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The timing is critical because it explains why Contracting will be a hot topic at TechIQ and why you need to own this conversation.

questions.question: What is the projected annual savings amount for high-volume sponsors using CTFS Contracting?
choices: $1.5 million
$3 million
$5 million
$7 million
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—$3 million in projected annual savings for sponsors running 100-plus trials per year, assuming two CTAs per site and 200 sites per trial.
questions.feedback_incorrect: This number applies specifically to high-volume sponsors (100+ trials per year) and reflects the cumulative cost of manual CTA processing that AI eliminates.

questions.question: When a buyer says 'we already have a system,' what does the course recommend you do?
choices: Immediately argue that CTFS is superior
Ask what gap their current system doesn't fill
Suggest they pilot CTFS alongside their existing system
Accept their objection and move to the next prospect
questions.feedback_correct: You've got the right approach—asking the gap question almost always opens a genuine conversation because the honest answer reveals real unmet needs.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course teaches that the gap question is more powerful than arguing features. It shifts the conversation from 'we're already set' to 'here's what we still struggle with.'

questions.question: What does the course identify as the key differentiator that separates CTFS from point-solution competitors?
choices: Better user interface design
Lower pricing than competitors
Unification across the entire financial lifecycle with automatic data flow between modules
Faster customer support response time
questions.feedback_correct: Spot on—the unification story is where CTFS wins, because a budget in GrantPlan automatically informs the contract, which triggers payments, which feeds forecasting with real data.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course emphasizes that point solutions solve one problem but create integration headaches elsewhere. Unification eliminates duplicate data entry and reconciliation friction.

questions.question: According to the course, what are the three milestone targets for a qualified 30-day follow-up plan?
choices: An email sent, a phone call made, and a brochure shared
A scheduled discovery call, a defined CRM opportunity with qualification criteria, or a pilot invitation accepted
A demo attended, a proposal sent, and a contract started
LinkedIn connection, email follow-up, and a second meeting
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—these three options give you concrete markers to track whether a follow-up is actually advancing the opportunity past interest into action.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course teaches that every follow-up needs a specific milestone target—something concrete on the calendar or in your CRM, not just a sense that someone was interested.

questions.question: What happens automatically when a CTA is signed in CTFS Contracting?
choices: A report is generated and sent to the finance team
Payment milestones in Site Payments and budget alignment in GrantPlan are updated without manual re-keying
An email notification goes to all stakeholders
The contract is archived in a secure folder
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—this automatic integration is exactly what makes Contracting not just a standalone tool but a critical piece of the unified platform.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course emphasizes that signed CTAs automatically inform both Site Payments milestones and GrantPlan budget updates, eliminating manual transfer and reconciliation.

questions.question: When should you capture your notes after a meaningful TechIQ conversation?
choices: At the end of the day when all conversations are fresh in your mind
Immediately after the conversation, within 90 seconds
Within 24 hours while details are still relatively fresh
During your follow-up call scheduled for the next week
questions.feedback_correct: You've got the timing exactly right—capturing insights immediately, even as a voice memo, prevents details from blending with the eight other conversations you'll have that day.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course is explicit: capture immediately, not at the end of the day. By then you'll have had multiple conversations and the specific details will blur together.
